claim.quote: we set a lower limit on the half-life of the neutrinoless double beta decay in 76Ge of T_1/2 > 5.7 * 10^{25} yr at 90% C.L., thus excluding an effective Majorana neutrino mass greater than 0.2 eV

date.locator: arXiv stamp on the first page
date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Phys. Rev. Lett. 83, 41 (1999).

key_value_text.quote: T_1/2 > 5.7 * 10^{25} yr at 90% C.L., thus excluding an effective Majorana neutrino mass greater than 0.2 eV
key_value_text.value: T1/2(0vbb, 76Ge) > 5.7e25 yr (90 % C.L.); effective Majorana neutrino mass < 0.2 eV

name: Limits on the Majorana neutrino mass in the 0.1 eV range

summary.plain: After 24 kg-years of data with pulse-shape selection, the Heidelberg-Moscow experiment saw no neutrinoless double beta decay in germanium-76. The half-life must exceed 5.7 x 10^25 years, which rules out an effective Majorana neutrino mass above 0.2 eV.
summary.technical: Pulse-shape-selected data, 24 kg y: T1/2(0vbb, 76Ge) > 5.7e25 yr at 90 % C.L., corresponding to <m_ee> < 0.2 eV for the matrix elements used; the full-spectrum 41.55 kg y set gave a weaker limit.

title: Limits on the Majorana neutrino mass in the 0.1 eV range
why_it_matters: One of the two most sensitive 76Ge searches of its time; its limit set the bar that the GERDA Phase I test of the later claim compared against.
